However, rather than stop at 'GEM-only entity', I fetched SNGPL's own official Transmission Network map (sngpl.com.pk, live page verified via url_verifier: OK/200; page links a georeferenced map image dated 'AS ON 30-06-2026') and visually inspected both the thumbnail and the full 4800x7200 high-res version (image link on that same page: images/transmission/TransmissionMap072026L.jpg). That map independently and directly confirms all three named points as real, connected nodes on SNGPL's live transmission network: 'Dakhni' (drawn as a compressor station, exact spelling match) sits just south of Kohat/Attock; it connects via an 8in line then a 24in line to a labelled 'Meyal Plant' node (a gas processing plant icon), which in turn connects via 8in/8in lateral branches and an 18in mainline down to 'Dhulian' (a large compressor-station hub, exact spelling match) — i.e. an actual mapped Dakhni->Meyal Plant->Dhulian corridor exists exactly as GEM's title states. (A second, parallel SNGPL corridor also links the same Dakhni cluster to Dhulian via an intermediate node called 'Ratana', diameters 16in/10in/16in — not named in GEM's title but physically adjacent; see the spec note below.) This is a single source, but it is the network operator's own current official asset map, which I weight higher than a typical single citation. Net: existence concern is resolved — this is real transmission infrastructure, not a phantom/hallucinated row — though the exact single-line specification GEM records doesn't map cleanly onto either real corridor (see spec finding).

validity.researcher_notes: Classification: the SNGPL map I inspected is titled 'Transmission Network' and shows Dakhni/Ratana/Dhulian as compressor stations on that network (same convention independently confirmed for a sibling roster row, P4157, whose shard notes SNGPL's own map labels even short single-customer feeder branches as part of its 'Transmission System') — so PipelineType='transmission' matches the utility's own usage, not a gathering-line misclassification. Fuel='Gas' is consistent with every source found: SNGPL's map is exclusively a natural-gas transmission map, and independently Business Recorder (brecorder.com, two articles, verified OK/200) describes Dhulian and Meyal as core Potatohar-basin gas/oil producing assets of Pakistan Oilfields Ltd (POL), while OGDCL press coverage (Daily Times and the state news agency APP, both verified OK/200) confirms Dakhni is an active OGDCL gas/condensate field/compression facility (a Feb-2026 'Dakhni Front End Compression Project' commissioning). Owner: the SNGPL map is literally the utility's own asset map, i.e. a first-party confirmation that SNGPL operates the compressor stations and pipe on this exact corridor - consistent with Owner1='Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Ltd (SNGPL)' 100%. Note the interesting wrinkle that upstream production at Dakhni is OGDCL's and at Meyal/Dhulian is POL's (two different E&P companies) while the connecting transmission pipe itself is SNGPL's - that is exactly how Pakistan's gas midstream is structured (SNGPL buys/gathers gas from multiple upstream producers into its own trunk system), so this is not a misattribution. Duplicate check against the given 63-row roster: no other row names Dakhni, Meyal, or Ratana; P4164 ('Dhulian-Daud Khel Gas Pipeline', 85.2 km, 8in) is a different, non-overlapping corridor running from the same Dhulian hub northward to Daudkhel/F3 (visible on the same SNGPL map as an 18in line south from Dhulian to 'Daudkhel F3') - a complementary segment, not a double-count of P4163.

validity.recommendation: Do not delete or fabricate a corrected number — but flag Diameter=16in for a targeted follow-up. On SNGPL's own map, the segments that literally run Dakhni -> Meyal Plant -> Dhulian (the route matching GEM's title) are labelled 8in (Dakhni link), 24in (Dakhni-Meyal Plant), and 18in (Meyal Plant-Dhulian mainline) - NOT 16in. A 16in diameter DOES appear in the immediate area, but on the parallel, unnamed-in-GEM corridor via 'Ratana' (Dakhni-Ratana 16in, Ratana-Dhulian 16in/10in). So either GEM's row is a composite/aggregate of the two real parallel corridors and picked the wrong one's diameter, or the 16in value belongs to a distinct, currently-unlisted 'Dakhni-Ratana-Dhulian' segment. Length (50.44 km) could not be independently checked at all - the map has no scale bar in the region I could locate, and I found no OGRA/SNGPL document giving a line-item length for this specific corridor. Recommend a follow-up against SNGPL's internal line register (not published) or an OGRA State of the Regulated Petroleum Industry annex before treating either number as verified; leaving the values as-is for now rather than guessing a replacement.
validity.researcher_notes: Full detail: I fetched and visually read SNGPL's official Transmission Network map (dated AS ON 30-06-2026, images/transmission/TransmissionMap072026L.jpg linked from the verified sngpl.com.pk Transmission System page) at full resolution around the Kohat/Attock/Dhulian cluster. Two separate, parallel SNGPL corridors run between the Dakhni-Kohat cluster and the Dhulian hub: (A) Dakhni -> Ratana -> Dhulian, diameters 16in / 10in / 16in; (B) Dakhni -> Meyal Plant -> Dhulian, diameters 8in / 24in / 8in(lateral) / 18in. GEM's row is named for corridor (B) (it names 'Meyal', not 'Ratana') but its recorded Diameter (16in) matches corridor (A) instead. I could not find any independent source stating a single length or diameter for a unified 'Dakhni-Meyal-Dhulian' line as GEM presents it - the map itself doesn't merge the two corridors into one named line, and no news/regulatory source I found gives line-item specs for either. This is a genuine spec disagreement worth flagging per the corroboration rule (a source must AGREE with the GEM number, not just mention the area) - I am not proposing a replacement number because I don't have a source stating the correct one either, only evidence that 16in belongs to a different (Ratana) segment than the one GEM's title describes.
